subject: Warmup starvation impacting BrightRetail reserved pool
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@brightretail.com>, ops@brightretail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 09:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Warmup starvation impacting BrightRetail reserved pool

Hi Alex / BrightRetail ops team,

Quick note to let you know we're seeing a warmup starvation pattern in your reserved GPU pool that is degrading short-lived high-concurrency requests during business hours. We observed a sustained drop in throughput for requests that rely on cold KV-cache fetches — latency increases from ~120ms p50 to 900–1,200ms p95 for 1–3s generation requests.

Impact summary:
- Scope: BrightRetail reserved pool (single-region, us-west-2)
- Symptom: extended per-request latency spikes for bursty small-gen traffic; concurrent warmup tasks are getting deprioritized by the local allocator
- User-visible: intermittent degraded page load times for product detail widgets and cart recommendations (estimated ~12% of requests during peak)

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Elevated to on-call infra and pinned the pool to conservative batching settings
- Enabled a temporary routing rule to divert ~20% of traffic to a compatible hosted variant to protect latency-sensitive requests
- Collected warmup traces and live log slices (attached)

Short-term ask: can you confirm if there were any deployment changes or workload pattern changes starting 2028-05-22 08:30 PDT? That will help us correlate.

We're preparing a remediation plan and a proposed customer credit for impacted minutes; I will follow up with a concrete remediation timeline within 4 hours.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll take ownership of remediation and the post-incident analysis.

Best,
Hannah
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: warmup-logs-20280522.txt (text)]

From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@brightretail.com>

Thanks Hannah — we saw the same latency blips on our end and had a handful of customers open support tickets. No deployments from our side since early morning, but we did launch a higher-concurrency A/B test at 07:45 PDT which increased short-lived inference calls.

Can you share the ETA for a fix and whether this reroute will cause any consistency differences in model outputs for our recommender service? Also please share the scope of the credit you're proposing so I can flag for procurement.

— Alex
Head of Ops, BrightRetail

Subject: Re: Warmup starvation impacting BrightRetail reserved pool

Alex / team — adding technical details and an interim mitigation we can apply now.

Root cause (current hypothesis):
- The serving allocator is prioritizing long-lived batched streams; concurrent short-lived requests suffer because warmup jobs that populate KV-cache are being queued behind high-throughput workers.
- Your recent A/B test increased short-lived traffic by ~3.8x concentrated across a 15-minute window, which amplified warmup contention.

Immediate mitigations we recommend (can be applied in <30 minutes):
1) Enforce targeted warmup priority: bump warmup worker priority for BrightRetail reserved pool (non-disruptive)
2) Narrow reroute: increase hosted fallback to 35% only for user-facing endpoints with a dedicated Content-SHA check to keep output parity
3) Short-term autoscaler tweak: lower scale-down aggressiveness to maintain more warm instances during peak hours

I've attached the live trace samples and a trimmed runbook snippet showing the exact cli commands. We can apply 1) and 3) now; need Alex to authorize the 35% reroute for user-facing endpoints.

Attachments: warmup-logs-20280522.txt, warmup-runbook.pdf

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@brightretail.com>, ops@brightretail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 May 2028 13:47:02 -07:00
Subject: Action plan & credit proposal for BrightRetail warmup impact

Alex — thanks for the quick context. We're applying the mitigations Marissa outlined now. Summary of what you'll see in the next 60–120 minutes: 

Planned timeline (today):
- T+0–30m: bump warmup worker priority and lower scale-down aggressiveness (no restart required)
- T+30–120m: increase hosted fallback to 35% for user endpoints with Content-SHA check (to preserve parity)
- T+120–240m: monitor for recurrence; if we still see p95 > 700ms we'll schedule a temporary capacity burst (reserved warm nodes) for 4 hours

Customer credit proposal: 
- We propose a service credit of 2% of the monthly committed fee for daily impact windows (calculated pro rata for the 3.5 hours of elevated impairment we observed in the morning). The attached PDF shows a worked example for your current commitment (Deal BR-45321).

Operational notes on parity: the hosted fallback uses the same quantized model variant with identical decoding configs. We will run a small side-by-side validation job and share the diff report by EOD. Expected delta: negligible for recommendation ranking (top-5 Jaccard > 0.96 across sampled queries).

Next steps / asks from BrightRetail:
- ACK the 35% reroute for user-facing endpoints (ops@brightretail.com)
- Share any changes to A/B test schedules for the next 48 hours so we can avoid repeated contention

We will follow with a short incident report and a technical postmortem by next Wednesday.

Attachments: credit-proposal-BR-45321.pdf

Thanks,
Hannah
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
